newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sets record final 1995/96 wheat, barley prices.
newsitem.headline: CWB sets record final 1995/96 wheat, barley prices.

text.p: Record final prices for Prairie wheat, durum, feed and malt barley were set on Friday for crop year 1995/96 (Aug/July) by the Canadian Wheat Board.
"The 1995/96 crop year saw CWB pool returns reach their highest levels ever. Total sales revenue on grain delivered to all four pool accounts reached a record C$5.8 billion," the CWB said.
Malt barley posted record prices and volume in 1995/96 when 2.5 million tonnes sold for C$620 million. The last record was in 1994/95 when 2.26 million tonnes sold for C$392 million.
Durum wheat sales volume was down in 1995/96 compared to the previous year but revenues reached a record C$1.1 billion.
Final CWB prices are set after the crop year is over and each commodity account is closed.

Canada's federal government approves and guarantees an initial, or first down payment, at the outset of the crop year which is usually 70 to 80 percent of the CWB's estimate of world grain values at that time.
Adjustment payments approved by the federal government are at times announced during the crop year as they were in 95/96. Final payment checks will be mailed the week of Dec 30.
